market_holds: Spot 3.31 at the 18:09 UTC seal (Yahoo; the last Yahoo bar shows 3.33 intraday on 11-11). Run-up +6.8% over 5 days and +8.2% over 20 days, 40% below the 52-week high. No usable option chain, so there is no implied move. My own count from Yahoo bars puts the last four prints at close to next open of -6.3% (Q2, 08-11), -1.8% (Q1), 0.0% (Q4'25) and +3.5% (Q3'25). Liquidity is thin, about 54k shares (~$180k) a day. The bar is consensus Q3 revenue of $146.6m and EPS of $0.08, from the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-03, against the company's own 'at least $145.7m' guide. The FY26 guide is revenue $565.5-577.8m and adj. EBITDA margin 15-17%, cut from 17-19% in August, set at an assumed BRL/USD of 5.17. H1 margin was 14.2%, so H2 needs about 15.7% to hit the low end. The preview frames the print on margin recovery, not on revenue. The stock fell 7.8% on 10-26, the day of the Lula-election BRL plunge, and has since recovered above its pre-election level.
view: A coin flip with a small upward tilt that I would not bet on. Q3 FX was neutral to the guide: BRL averaged 5.14 against the 5.17 assumed (FRED DEXBZUS). So the revenue line is the usual beat of the company's own 'at least' guide; Q2 came in at 142.8 against 140, which points to about $148m here. The margin is what matters. Q3 needs a visible step up from 13.3%, and Q2 showed the market will open the stock down 6% on a margin/EPS miss even with a revenue beat, before recovering by the close. Three things since the last call lean mildly positive. First, a cluster of small open-market insider purchases (Form 4 code P): the CEO, the North America president and a director bought from 09-10 to 10-09, including after quarter-end. Second, EPAM's strong Q3 (+7% on 11-05). Third, BRL has weakened to about 5.47 since 10-26, which helps the Q4 margin on a Brazil cost base. Weighing against them: the weaker BRL also cuts Q4 USD revenue, since Brazil is 50% of revenue. A headline trim of the USD revenue guide is plausible, and so is caution on Brazilian client spending after the election and 15% local yields. The 5-day run-up into the print has already taken part of the good news. Net: no line I can show the price has missed.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is the Q3 adj. EBITDA margin and whether the 15-17% FY margin guide holds. I found no dated datapoint that pins it either way. FX was neutral in Q3, and the Q4 FX effect cuts both ways (margin up, USD revenue down). The modest positives (insider buying, EPAM read-through) are partly in the 6.8% five-day run-up.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 margin of 16% or more with the FY margin guide reaffirmed, or raised on the weaker BRL, would make a long case. A margin under 14.5%, or a cut to the USD revenue guide framed as Brazil demand rather than FX, would make a short one.

self_critique: The insider buying came after quarter-end from three insiders, and the market reads a weaker BRL as a margin tailwind (the stock recovered fully after 10-26). A clean margin beat with a reaffirmed guide on a thin, cheap, 40%-off-high stock could gap +8-10% at the open. That argues for a long tilt larger than mine. Against that, the Q2 precedent of a -6% open on a margin miss shows the opening print punishes margin misses hard. My tilt is therefore a slight lean, not a call.
approach_notes: Rebuilding FX from FRED against the company's own stated assumption was the most useful step; it showed Q3 FX is neutral. The Form 4 route is new for this FPI and worked. The decisive line (Q3 margin) had no public trace before the print, so the playbook's stop-early rule applied.
